title: Allevia: generous living in dense Mont'Kiara.
excerpt: Careful tower placement, expressive architecture and spacious three-bedroom homes make a strong own-stay case in a competitive address.
takeaways: Mont'Kiara's schools, shops and international community support both own-stay and rental demand.
Sean praises the building's arrival sequence, tower spacing and wide horizontal unit layouts.
New supply, a future road connection and modest facilities complicate the premium proposition.

sections.heading: Why Mont'Kiara still works
paragraphs: Sean begins with the address. International schools, commercial centres, restaurants, gyms and services create a neighbourhood where many daily needs can be met without a long drive. A large expatriate community also supports demand for comfortable rental homes.

Allevia sits between Jalan Kiara 3 and Jalan Kiara 4. That dual frontage places it close to activity while the towers are arranged to preserve as much distance and outlook as possible within a dense high-rise district.

sections.heading: Architecture with room to breathe
paragraphs: The arrival sequence leaves the strongest first impression: fabric-like columns, considered lighting, step-free movement and a spacious lobby create an identity distinct from neighbouring projects. The landscaped deck uses playful forms even though its list of facilities remains conventional.

Inside, Sean favours the broad horizontal plan. The living and dining spaces sit together, the bedrooms are grouped to the sides, and generous in-between spaces make the roughly 1,900-square-foot three-bedroom unit feel composed rather than crowded.

sections.heading: Privacy, connectivity and competition
paragraphs: A proposed connection between Jalan Kiara 3 and Jalan Kiara 4 could make some journeys easier, but it may also remove the quiet, dead-end character valued by current residents. Sean treats that as a real trade-off rather than an automatic improvement.

He also points to continuing apartment supply in Mont'Kiara. The rental figures discussed in the video refer to the recording period and specific units; present-day prices and achievable rents require fresh evidence.

pros: Mont'Kiara's international schools, mature amenities and expatriate community make the address practical for own stay and established for rental demand.
Strong tower spacing, a memorable lobby and expressive material details give Allevia a distinctive architectural experience.
The wide three-bedroom layout devotes meaningful space to living, dining, kitchen and circulation instead of compressing every room.
cons: Mont'Kiara continues to receive substantial new supply, so buyers need to compare competing projects and rental evidence carefully.
The planned road connection may improve access while reducing the privacy of the current dead-end street.
The facilities are relatively conventional and minimal for this price category, despite attractive landscape treatment.

closing: Allevia's strongest argument is the quality of its everyday spaces. Its value still depends on how much a buyer prizes the address, generous layout and design over a longer facilities checklist.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full public English captions and published YouTube episode notes. The 3 on 3 section paraphrases the three strengths and three concerns Sean presents in the closing portion of the episode.
